body_ar:
ما هي عقيدة الأشعري ؟

أن الأشعري أبا الحسن علي بن إسماعيل من ذرية أبي موسى الأشعري هو من أئمة الدين ومن المحدثين والأصوليين والقراء، وقد اجتهد في بعض أمور الدين فأصاب في بعضها وأخطأ في بعضها، فما اجتهد فيه من العقائد بعضه صواب لا غبار عليه وبعضه خطأ بين واضح،

فلذلك لا حرج في تقليده في الصواب الذي أصاب فيه في حق من لا يعرف الدليل ولا يستطيعه، ولا يجوز تقليده فيما أخطأ فيه في حق من عرف أنه خطأ وهذا أيضا هو مذهب الأشعري وهو مذهب كل مجتهد من المجتهدين من أهل الدين، يرون موافقتهم فيما وافق الشرع ويرون عدم تقليدهم فيما خالف الشرع لدى الإنسان نفسه،

فالخطاب الذي تخاطب به بين يدي الله ليس مقتضى عقل الأشعري ولا عقل مالك ولا عقل الشافعي، إنما تخاطب على مقتضى عقلك أنت، وما بلغك من الشرع، فما ترجح لديك لا تعذر في تركه ولو خالفه جمهور الناس، إذا ترجح لديك أن هذا النص ثابت عن رسول الله (ص) وفهمته بمقتضى اللغة وأنت من أهل الفهم في الشرع فهمته فهما لا يحل لك تركه بما لم تعرف دليله، ولو أتاك الأشعري نفسه وخاطبك بذلك، أو أتاك مالك وخاطبك به لا يحل لك العدول عن الدليل إذا عرفته،

فلذلك لا يقال: عقيدة الأشعري باطلة مطلقا ولا صحيحة مطلقا بل هي اجتهادات فيها صواب وفيها خطأ، والذي ذكره أهل العلم من أخطائه أربعة أخطاء فقط، وقد ذكر هو رجوعه عنها في كتاب مقالات الإسلاميين، وقد قال الحكماء قديما كفى المرء نبلا أن تعد معايبه، إذا كان الأشعري مجتهدا واجتهد في كثير من الاجتهادات فأخطأ في أربعة فقط ورجع عنها فهذا يكفيه فخرا ويكفيه دليلا على الاستقامة أنه رجع عما تبين له خطؤه فيه،

ولذلك فإنه يقول في كتاب مقالات الإسلاميين كلما أتى إلى مقالة من المقالات التي كان له فيها مذهب ورجع عنه يذكر قول أهل الحديث وأهل السنة ثم يقول وبقولهم أقول، وهذا رجوع صريح من أبي الحسن رحمه الله إلى ذلك القول، وقد بين ذلك في مقدمة كتاب الإبانة أيضا وصرح به،

وعموما فكثير من الأقوال التي تنسب إلى أبي الحسن والتي يراها الناس من مذهبه وهي مدونة في كتب الأشاعرة لا صلة لأبي الحسن الأشعري بها، لا يقولها أبدا بوجه من الوجوه، فمثلا مسألة الأحوال التي هي من أعظم المسائل التي خاض فيها الأشاعرة، قد نص الأشاعرة جميعا على أن أبا الحسن لا يراها، وأنه يخالفهم فيها، ومسألة إثبات صفة مستقلة تسمى الوجود وهي الصفة النفسية وهي مسألة لدى المتأخرين من الأشاعرة يصرحون بأن أبا الحسن ينكرها، ولذلك قال المقري في الإضاءة: ومن يرى الوجود عين الذات** كالشيخ لم يعدده في الصفات

وأيضا فإن كثيرا من الأقوال المنسوبة إلى أبي الحسن لا تصح نسبتها إليه بوجه من الوجوه، كما يتعلق بالتقليد في أصول الدين، ولذلك قال السيوطي رحمه الله: يمتنع التقليد في العقائد** للفخر والأستاذ ثم الآمدي والعنبري جوزه وقد حظر** أسلافنا كالشافعي فيه النظر ثم على الأول إن يقلد** فمؤمن عاص على المعتمد لكن أبو هاشم لم يعتبر** إيمانه وقد عزي للأشعري قال القشيري عليه مفترى** فهذا القول نسبته إلى أبي الحسن الأشعري افتراء على أبي الحسن ليس من كلامه، قال القشيري عليه مفترى** والحق إن يأخذ بقول من عرى بغير حجة لأدنى وهم** لم يكفه ويكتفي بالجزم

هذا في الكوكب الساطع في نظم جمع الجوامع للسيوطي، لم يقل بذلك أبو الحسن قط، لم يقل بنفي العلو ولا قال إن الله في كل مكان أبدا ما قال هذا النوع من الكلام، بل قد نص على أن أئمة السلف نصوا على أن من قال إن الله في الأرض أو أنه في كل مكان فقد كفر.
body_en:
What is the creed of al-Ashari?

Al-Ashari — Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Ismail, of the progeny of Abu Musa al-Ashari — is one of the imams of the religion, and one of the hadith scholars, the legal theorists and the Qur'an reciters. He exercised independent legal reasoning (ijtihād) in some matters of religion, and was right in some of it and wrong in some of it. Of what he reasoned out in the doctrines of creed, some is correct beyond reproach, and some is plain and evident error.

For that reason there is no objection to following him (taqlīd) in what he got right, in the case of one who does not know the evidence and is not capable of it; and it is not permissible to follow him in what he got wrong, in the case of one who knows that it is wrong. This too is al-Ashari's own position, and it is the position of every one of the mujtahids among the people of religion: they hold that one should agree with them in what agrees with the revealed law, and hold that one should not follow them in what conflicts with the revealed law in the person's own view.

For the address by which you are addressed before God is not what al-Ashari's intellect requires, nor Malik's intellect, nor al-Shafi'i's intellect; you are addressed according to what your own intellect requires, and according to what of the revealed law has reached you. So whatever is preponderant in your view, you are not excused for abandoning it, even if the generality of people should oppose it. If it is preponderant in your view that this explicit text (naṣṣ) is established from the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, and you have understood it as the language requires — and you are one of the people of understanding in the revealed law and have understood it in a certain way — it is not lawful for you to abandon it for something whose evidence you do not know. Even if al-Ashari himself came to you and addressed you with that, or Malik came and addressed you with it, it is not lawful for you to turn aside from the evidence once you know it.

For that reason it is not said that al-Ashari's creed is void absolutely, nor that it is sound absolutely; rather they are exercises of reasoning, in which there is what is right and what is wrong. What the scholars have mentioned of his errors is four errors only, and he himself mentioned his retraction of them in the book Maqālāt al-Islāmiyyīn. The sages said of old: 'It is nobility enough for a man that his faults can be counted.' If al-Ashari was a mujtahid, and exercised his reasoning in many matters, and erred in four only and then retracted them, this is glory enough for him, and proof enough of his uprightness that he retracted what became clear to him to have been his error.

That is why, in the book Maqālāt al-Islāmiyyīn, whenever he comes to one of the positions in which he had held a view and then retracted it, he mentions the position of the people of hadith and the people of the sunnah and then says: 'and it is their view that I hold.' This is an explicit retraction by Abu al-Hasan, may God have mercy on him, in favour of that position; and he made it clear and stated it expressly in the introduction to the book al-Ibānah as well.

In general, many of the positions that are attributed to Abu al-Hasan, which people take to be of his school and which are recorded in the books of the Asharis, have no connection with Abu al-Hasan al-Ashari; he never said them at all, in any way. The question of the 'states' (aḥwāl), for example, which is one of the greatest questions the Asharis entered into: the Asharis have all stated expressly that Abu al-Hasan does not hold it and that he differs from them in it. And the question of affirming an independent attribute called 'existence' — the attribute of the self (al-ṣifah al-nafsiyyah) — is a question in which the later Asharis state expressly that Abu al-Hasan denies it. That is why al-Muqri said in al-Iḍāʾah: *And whoever holds existence to be the very self, like the Shaykh, has not counted it among the attributes.*

Also, many of the positions ascribed to Abu al-Hasan cannot correctly be ascribed to him in any way — as with what concerns following a scholar in the foundations of religion. That is why al-Suyuti, may God have mercy on him, said: *Following a scholar in the doctrines of creed is impermissible, in the view of al-Fakhr, the Ustadh, and then al-Amidi; al-Anbari allowed it; and our predecessors, like al-Shafi'i, barred speculation in it. Then, on the first view, if he does follow a scholar, he is a sinful believer, on the relied-upon view; but Abu Hashim did not reckon his faith as faith, and this has been ascribed to al-Ashari. Al-Qushayri said: it is a fabrication against him.* So this position — its ascription to Abu al-Hasan al-Ashari is a fabrication against Abu al-Hasan; it is not his words. *Al-Qushayri said: it is a fabrication against him. And the truth is that if he takes the view of one who is bare of any proof, on the strength of the slightest conjecture, it does not suffice him; and he is sufficed by certainty.* This is in al-Kawkab al-Sāṭiʿ, al-Suyuti's versification of Jamʿ al-Jawāmiʿ.

Abu al-Hasan never held that. He did not hold the denial of God's highness, nor did he ever say that God is in every place; he never said this kind of thing at all. On the contrary, he stated expressly that the imams of the salaf stated expressly that whoever says that God is in the earth, or that He is in every place, has fallen into unbelief.

flags.arabic: والذي ذكره أهل العلم من أخطائه أربعة أخطاء فقط، وقد ذكر هو رجوعه عنها في كتاب مقالات الإسلاميين
flags.context: the Sheikh's account of al-Ashari's four errors and his retraction of them
options: publish as given, with the four errors left unnamed as the Sheikh leaves them
publish with a note from the Sheikh's office on the historiographical point
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW ADVISED (style guide §12). The relation between Abu al-Hasan al-Ashari and later Ashari theology is a live and contested subject, and this answer takes clear positions in it: that his errors number exactly four, that he retracted them, and that much of what stands in Ashari books is falsely ascribed to him. It has been translated exactly as given and nothing has been added. Note for display that the Sheikh does NOT name the four errors, and an English reader will expect them; nothing has been supplied.

flags.arabic: al-Suyuti's four lines on taqlīd in creed, with the Sheikh's gloss inserted into them
flags.context: يمتنع التقليد في العقائد** للفخر والأستاذ ثم الآمدي … قال القشيري عليه مفترى** فهذا القول نسبته إلى أبي الحسن الأشعري افتراء … قال القشيري عليه مفترى** والحق إن يأخذ بقول من عرى بغير حجة لأدنى وهم لم يكفه ويكتفي بالجزم
options: render as prose in italics, with the Sheikh's prose gloss shown between the two halves as the source has it
render the verse whole first and place the gloss after it
leave the verse untranslated and carry only the Sheikh's gloss
flags.note: Dense usul verse from al-Kawkab al-Sāṭiʿ, quoted from memory, and the source repeats the hemistich قال القشيري عليه مفترى on either side of the Sheikh's own interjection. That structure has been kept. The last line (والحق إن يأخذ بقول من عرى بغير حجة لأدنى وهم لم يكفه ويكتفي بالجزم) is the most uncertain: it has been read as 'if he adopts the view of one who has no proof, on the slightest conjecture, that does not suffice him; certainty does suffice'. A reviewer with the printed naẓm should confirm, since it states what is required of an ordinary believer in matters of creed.

flags.context: ولذلك قال المقري في الإضاءة: ومن يرى الوجود عين الذات** كالشيخ لم يعدده في الصفات
options: al-Muqri, as the source spells the name, in al-Iḍāʾah
al-Maqqari in Iḍāʾat al-dujunnah fī ʿaqāʾid ahl al-sunnah
flags.note: The work is in all likelihood Iḍāʾat al-dujunnah fī ʿaqāʾid ahl al-sunnah by Ahmad al-Maqqari al-Tilimsani, a versified creed well known in the Maghribi and Shinqiti curriculum. The source's unvowelled المقري has been followed rather than an identification supplied, per style guide §11.

options: following a scholar in the doctrines of creed is impermissible
following a scholar in the doctrines of creed is barred
following a scholar in the doctrines of creed is ruled out
flags.note: NOTE ON §8. يمتنع here attaches to an act (taqlīd) and is therefore a legal judgement, not the kalām modality mumtaniʿ ('rationally impossible') that §8 of the style guide governs. The distinction matters in this file precisely because its subject is creed: a reader or a later reviser must not re-read this as the modal term. Likewise لا يجوز تقليده earlier in the answer is legal ('it is not permissible'), not modal.

translator_notes: Hadith and verse renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

The Sheikh distinguishes carefully throughout between Abu al-Hasan al-Ashari's own positions and what the later Asharis hold or ascribe to him. Every one of those attributions has been kept visibly distinct in the English, since the whole answer turns on them.
He does not name the four errors, and does not say which position of al-Ashari's al-Muqri's line is about beyond what the line itself says. Nothing has been supplied for either.

The lines of verse are rendered as prose in italics per house style; the source marks the hemistich break with a double asterisk. The Arabic should be displayed alongside, since the subject matter is technical.

بطلان and صحة here concern the validity of positions, not their moral status: باطلة مطلقا is rendered 'void absolutely' and صحيحة مطلقا 'sound absolutely', per the glossary entries for bāṭil and ṣaḥīḥ.

The closing sentence reports what al-Ashari said the imams of the salaf said; the chain of attribution is two deep in the Arabic and has been kept that way rather than flattened into the Sheikh's own voice.
